source_text: Eademque securitate, qua pedes et genua, etiam genitalia utriusque sexus vocantur. Nos sane nec cum ista suffragetur auctoritas, pudentioris eloquii adminicula negleximus; quia reprehensioni iustissimae patet, sine ullo negotiorum coactu neglectus decoris, qui non minus in verbis quam in operibus, quantum pertulerit causae ratio, retinendus est. Igitur quia concupiscentia naturalis nec pudoris opprobrio potuit coargui, et Conditoris sui dignitate defensa est, ad hoc solum, non ut quasi magnum bonum, quippe quod sit hominibus pecoribusque commune, sed quasi necessarium sexibus instrumentum, a iure daemonum vindicata, inter eius opera locaretur, qui mundum fecit et corpora, a nullo autem accusatur, nisi a Manichaeo, et Traduciano eius haerede; apparet naturalis peccati, cuius omne praesidium in naturae criminationibus haerebat, totum evanuisse figmentum.
pass_a_gloss: And with the same security with which feet and knees, even the genitals of each sex are named. We to be sure, not even when that authority suffrages, have neglected the supports of a more modest speech; because neglect of becomingness without any compulsion of businesses lies open to most just blame, which must be retained no less in words than in works, as far as the reason of the cause has borne. Therefore because natural desire could not be convicted by the reproach of modesty, and was defended by the dignity of its Founder, for this alone, not as a great good, seeing that it is common to humans and cattle, but as a necessary instrument for the sexes, having been claimed from the demons' right, it would be placed among the works of him who made the world and bodies, but is accused by no one except by Manichaeus and his heir the Traducian; it appears that the whole fiction of natural sin, whose whole protection was sticking in accusations of nature, has vanished.

lemmas.lexica: Julian's polemic label for teachers of tradux peccati
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: The genitals of both sexes are named as freely as feet and knees. Yet even with this authority supporting me, I have not neglected the aids of more modest speech. Neglect of decency without any compulsion from the subject lies open to the most just criticism. Decency should be maintained in words no less than in actions, as far as the subject allows. Natural desire, then, could not be convicted by the reproach of shame and has been defended by its Creator’s dignity. The purpose was not to treat it as some great good, since it is shared by human beings and animals, but as a necessary instrument of the sexes: rescued from the demons’ jurisdiction and placed among the works of the one who made the world and bodies. No one accuses it except Manichaeus and his heir, the advocate of inherited sin. It is therefore evident that the entire fiction of natural sin has vanished, since its whole support depended on accusations against nature.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
